answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with quadratic voting: each verified identity, say Ember, Violet or Cedar, receives a fixed credit budget, and casting n votes on one decision costs n squared credits. Splitting a fixed budget among many fake agents makes the sum of squares explode, so an attacker who clones itself pays far more per unit of influence than one honest agent. Every extra Sybil identity raises the cost while shrinking sway, making the attack uneconomic.
